title: Advanced Control Techniques for Wide-Speed-Range Sensorless Permanent Magnet Motor Drives
content: Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) drives employing sensorless control offer reduced cost, improved reliability and increased power density by eliminating mechanical position sensors. However, reliable operation from standstill to the field-weakening region remains challenging because of startup synchronization difficulties, electromechanical oscillations, and rotor position estimation errors at high speeds. This paper proposes an Integrated Wide-Speed Sensorless Control Framework (IWSSCF) for wide-speed-range PMSM drives combining a low-loss closed-loop startup algorithm, an Electromechanical Oscillation Angle Compensation (EOAC) technique, a flux-observer-based Field-Oriented Control (FOC) scheme, and a stable field-weakening algorithm. During startup, the proposed controller minimizes the torque-producing current according to the estimated mechanical power demand while maintaining synchronization. The EOAC algorithm suppresses torque-angle oscillations and enables a smooth transition from open-loop to closed-loop sensorless operation, whereas the field-weakening strategy improves high-speed stability by mitigating the effects of transient rotor angle estimation errors. The proposed methodology is evaluated through detailed discrete-time simulations and validated experimentally using a laboratory PMSM drive. The obtained results demonstrate improved startup reliability, reduced power consumption, lower electromechanical oscillations and stable operation over the entire operating speed range. The proposed control framework therefore provides an efficient and robust sensorless solution for high-performance PMSM drive applications.
